 Follow Us On: News World No place for glorifying India: Posters beside defaced Tagore mural in Bangladesh No place for glorifying India: Posters beside defaced Tagore mural in Bangladesh
 Rabindranath Tagore's mural at Khulna Railway Station was defaced with black ink, while posters declaring there was "no place for glorifying India" appeared beside it. Police have launched an investigation.
 Advertisement Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore. (File image) By: India Today World Desk New Delhi , Nov 7, 2026 17:27 IST Last Updated Nov 7, 2026 17:27 IST Published by India Today Web Desk Nov 7, 2026 14:14 IST Edited by Tanu Jain A mural of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore was defaced with black ink in Bangladesh’s Khulna, while posters placed beside it accused him of hostility towards Muslims and East Bengal. Police have launched an investigation after residents noticed the damage on Friday morning.
 The mural is on the boundary wall of Khulna Railway Station, alongside portraits of prominent literary, cultural and political figures. The other portraits were left untouched, The Daily Star reported.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story One of the posters read: “There is no place for Tagore, who was hostile to Muslims and East Bengal, in Titumir’s Bengal. There is no place for glorifying India.” Rabindranath Tagore's Mural Defaced With Black Ink At Bangladesh 's Khulna Railway Station, Triggering Outrage Among Locals #RabindranathTagore #Bangladesh #Khulna #TagoreMural #MuralVandalism #BangladeshNews #CulturalHeritage #Tagore #Vandalism #SouthAsiaNews https://t.co/bJy9iCxPEC To get epaper daily on your whatsapp click here: https://t.co/0jgewcGGes— Free Press Journal (@fpjindia) November 7, 2026 POLICE INVESTIGATE VANDALISM
 Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Lokman Hossain said police learnt about the incident on Friday afternoon.
 “All businesses across the road were closed on Friday, making it difficult to determine who defaced the mural and when,” The Dhaka Tribune quoted him as saying.
 The Khulna City Corporation had commissioned the artwork ahead of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to the city.
 The wall features portraits of Fakir Lalon Shah, painter SM Sultan, Kazi Nazrul Islam, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, former president Ziaur Rahman and Michael Madhusudan Dutta. It also depicts the July uprising, the Sundarbans, the Sixty Dome Mosque and the jute industry. CIVIC, CULTURAL FIGURES CONDEMN INCIDENT
 Khulna City Corporation Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju condemned the vandalism, saying the portraits were intended to encourage free thinking among children and adolescents.
 “By defacing the portrait, they have exposed their narrow-mindedness and sick mentality,” The Dhaka Tribune quoted him as saying.
 Cultural activist and Nattyalok general secretary Shariful Islam Salim alleged that an organised group was responsible and warned that other prominent figures could be targeted.
 “They have carried out similar acts in Dhaka as well. These incidents are being orchestrated deliberately. Those responsible must be identified and brought to justice,” he told The Daily Star.
 Salim said Tagore’s literature and philosophy had inspired generations to embrace free thought, secularism and human dignity.
 The incident follows the defacement of a Tagore mural in Dhaka in October. Police detained four people in that case, including State Dialogue Forum member secretary Al Nur Mohammad Ayash, according to The Daily Star. - Ends (With PTI inputs)
